catalog_quote: 2.1 Basic stress Patterns. The Mairasi phonological word consists of two to seven syllables. Words most commonly have two, three, or four syllables. Primary stress (') is on the penultimate syllable. Secondary stress (") on words longer than three syllables occurs on the first syllable. ... [3.] The syllable has an obligatory nucleus of one vowel. ... Phonetic Vowel glides and length are interpreted as two syllables (see Vowels). ... There are morphophonological exceptions which allow an antepenultimate stress or a word final CVV. These involve an object marker /-i/. ... [4.3] Phonetic vowel length greater than what normally occurs on the primary stress syllable occurs in four common environments. 1. Word finally. sources.quote: 'Word stress (accent) normally occurs on the next to the last syllable. u-RA-tu 'fish''. Also: 'Vowels are often lengthened within words. This is written as a double vowel. eete 'egg' in contrast with ete 'anchor'' (consistent with Peckham 1991's V.V two-syllable analysis of length).
